stories.headline: 5.1 magnitude earthquake hits Xinjiang near Ladakh border, tremors felt in J&K
stories.title: 5.1 magnitude earthquake hits Xinjiang near Ladakh border, tremors felt in J&K
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 5: An earthquake of magnitude 5.1 hit Xinjiang, China near the Ladakh border on Thursday night, with tremors felt in Jammu and Kashmir. According to primary data source GFZ/EMSC, the quake occurred at 10:26 pm on November 5, 2026. Its epicenter was located at 35.6°N latitude and 78.18°E longitude, at a depth of 83 km / 110 km. The tremors were felt in parts of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. However, no loss of life or damage to property has been reported so far. Further details are awaited. (GNS)

stories.headline: Rupee closes at a 2-month high on possibility of de-escalation West Asia war, softening crude, weak dollar
stories.title: Rupee closes at a 2-month high on possibility of de-escalation West Asia war, softening crude, weak dollar
stories.summary: Market watchers cited declining US yields, renewed risk appetite from foreign inflows, and bargain buying as the currency climbed for a fifth straight session, with eyes on nearby 94.00 support and 94.90 resistance
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The rupee (INR) closed at a two-month high on Thursday on expectations the US will de-escalate the Middle East war after the Democrats swept the midterm elections, falling US Treasury yields, softening crude oil prices and a weakening dollar.
The Indian unit closed at 94.47 per USD, a level last seen in early September, up 17 paise, against the previous close of 94.64.
Intraday, INR tested a high/low of 94.32/94.57.

Dilip Parmar, Senior Research Analyst, HDFC Securities, noted that the Indian rupee extended its northbound journey for the fifth consecutive session, supported by a declining US dollar and lower Treasury yields.
“Risk-on sentiment, driven by foreign fund inflows and softer crude oil prices, further underpinned the domestic currency.
Spot USD/INR retraced to its October lows, triggering some bargain buying in today’s session.
In the near term, the pair faces psychological support at 94.00, with resistance pegged at 94.90,” he said.

Axis Bank’s economic research team, comprising Tanay Dalal, Senior Vice President, and Vipul Jindal, Assistant Vice President, in a report, opined that the US political shifts with the blue wave (Democrat win in the mid-term elections) can directly impact INR fair value, as a retreat from the Middle-East conflict can improve terms of trade, a slower AI rollout can pull costs of capital lower and protect productivity.

However, the great power competition is unlikely to end, leading fiscal spending to continue (the national debt of major countries in conflicts tends to increase) and continuing to draw down on savings.
These have driven the financeable CAD (current account deficit) to 0 per cent and a basic balance deficit since 2023.
The estimates of the Bank’s economic research team show that fair value is still weaker than current levels, though depreciation of fair value may no longer outpace actual depreciation.
This is also visible in lower forwards and a smaller covered interest parity gap.

stories.title: Jagan accuses Naidu of ‘election subversion’, says TDP victory in ULB polls not people’s verdict
stories.summary: The ruling party manipulated the electoral process from nominations to counting by using the police and administrative machinery, alleges Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy; accuses State Election Commission of ‘’failing to function as an independent electoral authority’’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: YSR Congress Party president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy on Thursday accused Chief Minister and Telugu Desam Party (TDP) national president N. Chandrababu Naidu of ‘’compromising the credibility of democratic institutions for political gain by manipulating the recent local body elections and misusing official machinery’’.

Describing the alleged irregularities as “election subversion” and an “organised capture of democracy”, Mr. Jagan said Mr. Naidu would not have won had the elections been conducted in a free and fair manner.

Addressing a media conference at the YSRCP central office in Tadepalli near here, he alleged that the ruling party had manipulated the electoral process from nominations to counting by using the police and administrative machinery to eliminate opposition candidates and suppress dissent.
Mr. Jagan said Mr. Naidu had resorted to electoral manipulation because he lacked the confidence to face the electorate after failing to fulfil the promises made before the Assembly elections.
‘’Having failed to implement the Super.
Six, Super Seven and other assurances, the Chief Minister had chosen to undermine the electoral process rather than face the people,’’ he alleged.
The YSRCP president alleged that his party's candidates were prevented from filing nominations, forced to withdraw and subjected to arbitrary rejection of their papers.
He accused the police of colluding with TDP activists to intimidate opposition leaders and workers, while Returning.
Officers facilitated irregularities during scrutiny.
He also charged the State Election Commission with ‘’failing to function as an independent electoral authority and instead acting at the behest of the ruling establishment’’.
The institutions responsible for protecting democracy, including the police and administrative machinery, had lost public credibility, he alleged.
Citing incidents from across the State, Mr. Jagan alleged that YSRCP polling agents were forcibly removed from polling stations, confined in police stations and prevented from monitoring the process.

stories.headline: Delhi Police flagged unauthorised construction five months before Chawri Bazar building collapse that killed two
stories.title: Delhi Police flagged unauthorised construction five months before Chawri Bazar building collapse that killed two
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'building collapse' in title weight 46
article_sentences: The Delhi police had flagged unauthorised construction at a property in Chawri Bazar nearly five months before it collapsed on Thursday, killing at least two labourers.

A letter dated June 15, accessed by The Hindu, shows that the police had alerted the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to unauthorised construction at property numbers 4547-48 in Gali Sheesh Mahal, Ajmeri Gate, and sought necessary action.
The letter was addressed to the Deputy Commissioner of the erstwhile City-SP Zone, now Old Delhi Zone.
“I am to inform you that unauthorised construction is being carried out at the above-mentioned premises.
You are requested to inform the agencies concerned for necessary action at their end.
Necessary police assistance will be provided as and when required, except Fridays,” the letter stated.
Despite the warning, construction continued at the building, which collapsed while the shuttering of its third-floor roof was being removed, according to the MCD.
The roof had reportedly been completed about 15 days earlier.
The MCD initially maintained that it had received no complaints before the incident.
However, responding to the letter, it later said that “an inspection had been conducted, but repair work was found to be under way”.
A senior MCD official told.
The Hindu that no building plan had been sanctioned and no permission obtained for the construction.

stories.headline: US Treasury imposes fresh sanctions against Indian, Turkish entities for alleged Iran transactions
stories.title: US Treasury imposes fresh sanctions against Indian, Turkish entities for alleged Iran transactions
stories.summary: MEA says it has taken note of sanctions; not much can be done in case of entities supporting shadow fleets, sources said
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The US Treasury on Wednesday imposed fresh sanctions on individuals and companies based in India and Turkiye for allegedly supporting Iran’s oil and aviation sectors respectively.
The move came a day after Democrats made large gains in the midterm elections, winning control of both houses of Congress.
The sanctions fall under “Operation Economic Outcast,” the Trump administration’s effort to choke off Iran’s oil income and the funding it provides for the conflict with the US and Israel.
“We have taken note of the sanctions,” an official in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) told businessline.
Similar sanctions had also been imposed against Indian entities earlier this year, in August and in October.

“As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us…We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air,” Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent said in a Treasury statement issued on Wednesday.

Sources said there is not much that the Indian government could do about the situation as many such entities operated illegitimately and could be part of shadow fleet networks operated from cities such as Dubai.
“No legitimate Indian business imports oil from Iran.
They do not want to go against the US sanctions.
But there are shadow fleets that may be operating, often with bases in places such as Dubai, and the entities linked to these get into trouble,” a source tracking the matter explained.

In its latest operations, the US targeted the “vast criminal network” of India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma and his spouse, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, who allegedly supported Iran’s shadow fleet through a web of maritime fraud.

“Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies,” the Treasury noted.

stories.title: Cabinet approves 30-year lease of four acres in High Grounds to Bangalore Turf Club
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: With the racing activity held by the Bangalore Turf Club (BTC) expected to be relocated to Kunigal, the State government on Thursday approved the leasing of four acres on the current premises in High Grounds to the BTC for a period of 30 years.
The four-acre area currently houses the club facilities and includes a heritage structure.
While agreeing to shift racing activities to the Kunigal Stud Farm, the BTC had sought six acres to continue its club activities and off-course betting centre.
However, the government agreed to provide four acres.
Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre told presspersons after the Cabinet meeting that the government had approved the lease proposal.
“The club has also sought some time to relocate the racing activities to Kunigal,” he said.
The development follows an earlier decision by the State government not to extend the lease term to the BTC and its offer of land to build a racecourse at the Kunigal Stud Farm.
After initial reluctance, the BTC agreed to shift activities to Kunigal while seeking six acres to continue club operations and its off-course betting centre on the existing premises.
Mr. Khandre also announced that the winter session at Belagavi, scheduled to be held from November 30 to December 11, has been rescheduled to start from December 2.

stories.headline: UGC rules row: Centre mulls review panel, months after Supreme Court stay
stories.title: UGC rules row: Centre mulls review panel, months after Supreme Court stay
stories.summary: Modi government weighs changes to controversial equity regulations amid continuing legal and political scrutiny
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: - Centre considers committee to revisit UGC's controversial 2026 equity regulations.
- Supreme Court flags ambiguity, possible misuse and gaps in safeguards.
- BJP faces competing demands from general-category and reserved-category groups.

The Narendra Modi government is considering setting up a committee to review the controversial University Grants Commission (UGC) equity regulations, nearly 10 months after the Supreme Court stayed their implementation following a legal challenge over alleged discrimination against general-category students.

Solicitor-general Tushar Mehta informed a Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Thursday, 5 November, that the government was contemplating constituting a committee to examine the concerns surrounding the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026.
The submission came after the bench suggested that the Centre revisit the provisions and ensure that the interests of every student were protected.
The court granted the government four weeks before taking up the matter again.

The proposed committee could provide the Centre an opportunity to revisit the contentious provisions and work towards a revised framework without abandoning the stated objective of preventing caste discrimination in higher educational institutions.
The latest development is significant because the Centre had already informed the Supreme Court in August that it was reconsidering the regulations.
The proposal to constitute a committee now suggests that the government is moving towards a more structured review, although its composition, mandate and terms of reference are yet to be announced.
The controversy has placed the BJP in a politically uncomfortable position.
The regulations triggered protests among sections of the general-category electorate, including upper-caste groups that constitute an important part of the party's support base.

stories.title: Centre Supports Plea In Supreme Court Against Grant Of Perks To Judges Who Resign Amid Impeachment
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta on Wednesday submitted before the Supreme Court that the petitioner challenging the grant of perks and amenities to constitutional functionaries such as judges who resign to avoid removal proceedings appears to have a case.
“I will take instructions and respond.
I think the petitioner has a case.
The petitioner seems to have a case.
I will file a response,” Mehta told a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi.
The Court adjourned the matter, allowing the Union of India to file a counter affidavit.
The petition seeks to restrain the grant of perks, amenities, facilities and other entitlements to constitutional functionaries who resign from office to avoid proceedings for their removal.

stories.headline: Umar Khalid Moves Supreme Court Seeking Bail In Delhi Riots UAPA Case, Cites Near Expiry Of One Year Embargo
stories.title: Umar Khalid Moves Supreme Court Seeking Bail In Delhi Riots UAPA Case, Cites Near Expiry Of One Year Embargo
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Former JNU scholar Umar Khalid has moved the Supreme Court seeking bail in the 2020 Delhi riots larger conspiracy case after the Delhi High Court denied him bail recently.
He has submitted that the Supreme Court's one-year embargo imposed on the grant of bail was to expire soon.
He also said that the other condition imposed by the Court for examination of protected witnesses by the prosecution cannot possibly be completed by January 5, 2027.
Therefore, in light of prolonged incarceration, he be granted bail, the plea urged.

It may be recalled that on January 5, 2026, a bench comprising Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria denied bail to Imam and former JNU scholar Khalid, calling them "ideological drivers" of the larger conspiracy.
It, however, granted bail to five other accused persons, including Gulfisha Fatima, by distinguishing the roles played by them in the alleged conspiracy.

While denying bail, the Court imposed a one-year embargo on the grant of bail and stated that Imam and Khalid can approach the Court upon the completion of protected witnesses' examination or upon expiry of 1 year from passing the order, "whichever is earlier".
On September 30, a division bench of the Delhi High Court comprising Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Dinesh Bhatt denied bail on grounds that it can't modify the Supreme Court's order.

Khalid has stated that since the charges are yet to be framed and the prosecution has failed to examine witness, the Supreme Court's condition "whichever is earlier" can't be expected to take place within the outer limit of January 5, 2027.

The accused has also relied upon Justice Aravind Kumar's May 22 order referring the matter to larger bench on the "perceived conflict" among different benches of the Supreme Court in its interpretation of the KA Najeeb judgment, which held that a long period of incarceration can melt down the rigours of stringent bail provisions under UAPA.

The conflict occurred after a two-judge bench comprising Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Ujjal Bhuyan in Syed Ifthikar Andrabi criticised the Gulfisha Fatima judgment for taking a narrow view regarding bail in UAPA by diluting the verdict of Najeeb.

Considering the reservations expressed by Justice Nagarathna's bench, Justice Kumar's bench referred the matter to a larger bench while granting interim bail to co-accused Tasleem Ahmed and Khalid Saifi for six months.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks Trinamool MLA To Approach Calcutta HC For Expeditious Decision On Disqualification Pleas Against Rebel MLAs
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks Trinamool MLA To Approach Calcutta HC For Expeditious Decision On Disqualification Pleas Against Rebel MLAs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday disposed of a fresh petition filed by Trinamool Congress (TMC) MLA Sohandeb Chattopadhyay seeking expeditious adjudication of disqualification proceedings against 10 rebel party legislators, including West Bengal Leader of Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee, asking him to approach the Calcutta High Court.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi disposed of the petition, granting liberty to Chattopadhyay to file an appropriate plea before the High Court.
It requested the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to place the matter before a Division Bench for expeditious consideration and disposal.
“It seems to us that the appropriate recourse at this stage would be to approach the Calcutta High Court.
We dispose of the petition at this stage with liberty to the petitioner to file an appropriate petition before the High Court.
We request the Chief Justice of the High Court to place before a division who shall decide the matter expeditiously," the Court ordered.
The disqualification petitions were filed against 10 MLAs alleged to have defected after contesting the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections on TMC tickets.
They include Ritabrata Banerjee, Arup Roy, Firhad Hakim, Sandipan Saha, Akhruzzaman Ansari, Shiuli Saha, Sabina Yasmin, Biplab Mitra, Javed Khan and Rathin Ghosh.
The petition challenged the Speaker's October 8 orders issuing notices in the disqualification proceedings against the rebel MLAs.
Chattopadhyay sought intervention over the failure to decide the disqualification petitions within the timeframe indicated by the Supreme Court.
During the hearing, counsel for the petitioner submitted that the disqualification petitions were been filed on July 8 and nearly five months have elapsed without a decision.
She highlighted that the Supreme Court in its earlier order had requested the Speaker to decide the petitions by October 8.

stories.headline: Merchants Cannot Pass On UPI Charges To Customers, MDR Necessary To Sustain UPI Ecosystem : NPCI Tells Supreme Court
stories.title: Merchants Cannot Pass On UPI Charges To Customers, MDR Necessary To Sustain UPI Ecosystem : NPCI Tells Supreme Court
stories.summary: 96% of Person to Merchant transactions would remain free, the NPCI stated.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: 96% of Person to Merchant transactions would remain free, the NPCI stated.

Defending its decision to levy charges for transactions above ₹2,000 from individuals to merchants under the revised Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for Unified Payment Interface (UPI), the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has told the Supreme Court that merchants are barred from passing on MDR charges to customers.
It has further stated that UPI application providers cannot impose platform fees or other charges for UPI payments.

“Second, non-compliance by a Payer PSP or TPAP with the NPCI Circular's directive against passing on MDR to customers constitutes a breach of the binding obligation under the SLAs to abide by all circulars, orders, directions and instructions issued by the Answering Respondent, and exposes such Payer PSP or TPAP to compliance actions which may also lead to termination of its UPI membership and facilities.

Therefore, the non-pass-through directive to the banks and UPI service providers is a mandatory and binding direction, which is enforceable through contractual mechanism in place, and is not a mere 'assurance' or a matter of policy.
Thus, apprehension that the consumers are left exposed to an indirect burden is accordingly without any foundation”, the affidavit states.

NPCI has filed a counter affidavit filed on November 3 in a petition challenging the amendment to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, introduced through the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, the subsequent Ministry of Finance notification and the revised MDR framework announced in September.

The Supreme Court had in September 2026 sought an affidavit explaining the basis for the move to levy charges for transactions through Unified Payment Interface (UPI) above ₹2,000 from individuals to merchants.

NPCI has submitted that around 96% of person-to-merchant transactions will remain unaffected by the revised MDR, the NPCI has refuted the apprehension that the MDR charges would cause merchants to increase prices.

“The charge under the MDR is attracted only to a small fraction i.e. approximately 4%, of P2M transactions that exceed INR 2,000 and thus, a measure confined so narrowly in its incidence affords less scope for merchants to recalibrate their pricing across their entire customer base merely on account of a charge that arises only occasionally and only above a defined value.
Accordingly, the apprehension that the MDR Framework will result in quiet revision of prices is also misconceived”, the NPCI has stated.
NPCI has stated that person-to-person transactions and transactions involving small merchants under the P2PM category will continue to remain free.

stories.headline: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
stories.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
stories.summary: The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, a joint press release stated
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.
Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.

“The Foreign Secretary of India highlighted the wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation, and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India,” stated a joint press release issued by the Ministry of External Affairs and Kathmandu’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.
Mr. Shah had sought to involve other countries, such as the United Kingdom and China, in talks on the issue.
But India wants the matter to be resolved bilaterally.
The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

Mr. Misri’s discussions with Nepali stakeholders included a “commerce and development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties”, as well as new areas like digital connectivity and AI.
Mr. Misri also met Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.
Mr. Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister in March this year following the Gen-Z uprising in Nepal in September 2025 that led to the ouster of the previous government.
